subject: Dedicated capacity: H100 vs A100 vs L4 — decision path and clarifying questions
messages:

Cc: Ravi Singh <r.singh@nebulalabs.com>

Subject: Re: Quick follow-up: Dedicated plan and workload samples

Thanks David — attaching the samples we discussed (small set for privacy). High level: Nebula runs a mixed workload (70% low-latency chat, 30% large-batch embedding reindexing). Typical chat window: 2–4 tokens/sec per user, median context 1.5k, 95th ~8k. Embedding jobs are throughput-heavy but can be scheduled to off-peak.

Key asks from our side:
- Predictable p99 latency for chat under sustained peak (target <150ms token latency)
- Cost cap per million tokens for chat (we have internal threshold)
- Fallback plan when reserved capacity is saturated (we prefer graceful degradation rather than 503s)

I included: nebula_workload_samples.csv (anonymized traces) and a short doc with their internal SLOs. Happy to hop on a call if you need more detail.

—Elena

Hi Elena — thanks for the traces and SLOs, very helpful. A few clarifying Qs before we map to HW options:
1) What fraction of chat requests carry >4k context commonly?  (helps decide memory headroom vs tiling)
2) Are embedding jobs latency-sensitive or strictly best-effort nightly batches?
3) Any regulatory constraints for on-prem/private deployment (we may propose Dedicated with VPC)

Tentative thinking from our side:
- H100: best for large-context models where KV cache + memory headroom matter; higher perf per-seq but higher cost. Good p99 tail control for long-context chat.
- A100: solid middle ground for mixed workloads; cheaper than H100 for many configs but may require denser tiling or lower concurrency for very long contexts.
- L4: most cost-effective for short-context high-throughput chat and embedding throughput at smaller token sizes; limited memory for long context and KV.

I'll loop Ben/LAuren here for pricing/ops implications. If you can answer the Qs above, we can draft two concrete capacity maps: 1) latency-first (p99 focus) and 2) cost-first (target tokens/m$).

-David
David Kim

Hi all — answers inline:
1) ~8% of chat sessions hit >4k; 1.5% exceed 8k.
2) Embedding jobs are best-effort and scheduled (non-critical), though occasionally they run ad-hoc during business hours (we can gate them).
3) No special on-prem constraints right now; data residency within US is the requirement.

We'll prioritize p99 latency for chat; cost threshold is important but secondary to experience. Also curious about graceful degradation: could we route overflow to L4 instances (model-quantized variants) or fall back to slightly smaller context windows?

From: David Kim <david.kim@redwood.com>

Date: 2026-08-25T14:12:00-07:00
Subject: FW: Dedicated capacity follow-up — recommendation draft for NB-2026-442

Internal thread — summarizing next steps for the deal (NB-2026-442). Pulling a decision path together so AE/sales can present fast: 

Summary of external SLOs & constraints:
- Primary: p99 token latency <150ms for chat (peak sustained)
- 8% of sessions >4k, 1.5% >8k context
- Embeddings are non-latency-critical and can be scheduled
- Data residency: US-only (Dedicated w/ VPC ok)

Recommended decision path (2-tier):
1) Latency-first reserved pool (primary):
   - Mix of H100 and A100 nodes. Rationale: H100 nodes host long-context concurrent sessions (KV cache resident), A100 provides better tokens/$ for medium contexts and supports denser slotting for burst capacity.
   - Operational config: reserve 60% of committed slots as H100-optimized for models with >4k context; 30% A100 general pool; 10% L4 reserved for low-cost fallback and embeddings.
   - Autoscaling/burst: allow overflow to a metered burst pool (L4) with throttling rules and progressive degradation (truncate old history, reduce sampling temperature) to maintain p99 as much as possible.

2) Cost-first reserve (if Nebula asks to reduce commit):
   - Favor A100 primary with L4 burst for embeddings; H100 on-demand & scheduled windows for large-context heavy days.

Open technical notes / asks for Karthik:
- Confirm KV cache sizing assumptions for our H100 instance class given 8% >4k and 1.5% >8k (I sketched a headroom multiplier of 1.6x; need validation).
- Quantization/compatibility: which model variants do we recommend for L4 fallback? We should list model names & quant levels (FP16, 4-bit) and QoE expectations.
- Can ops support route-based fallback with per-request policy (route by model + priority)?

Ben/LAuren: please produce an updated cost projection (tokens/m$ across the 2-tier plan) and a slide we can take to Nebula with three clear options (latency-first commit, hybrid, cost-first commit). Attach the cost_model_h100_a100_l4.pdf overlay.

I'll take point for the customer call next Wed; Ben please be on pricing, Karthik please be on ops/tech.

-David
